reasons.A: Plain modern prose with even, short declaratives and no hedging asides or cataloguing rhythm; furthest from the author's discursive, period voice.
reasons.B: Period diction and use of 'one' fit, but its polished, balanced periodic sentences and urbane irony read more essayist-smooth than the author's loose, run-on catalogues.
reasons.C: Closest in movement: the repeated 'Take the matter of...' anaphora mirrors the author's 'It is an unusual thing' litany, with rambling lists and a chatty, confiding stance, though its closing quips are a touch neater than the author.
reasons.D: Hedges ('I dare say', 'as far as I could make out', 'so to speak'), a contraction and an exclamation catch the author's casual, confiding manner, but the sentences run more evenly and lack the repetitive listing drive.
